subject: Close runway replan — risk corridor and rollback options
messages:
From: Lisa Ortega <lisa.ortega@acmehealth.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Eli Navarro <eli.navarro@partnercloud.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Eval window issues — possible go-live push?

Hannah,

Quick note from our side: the evaluation run this morning surfaced two issues that materially affect our acceptance criteria.

1) Data parity: several read-only queries returned inconsistent row counts between our staging export and the live subset (see attached acme-eval-logs.csv).
2) Load profile: concurrent traffic in the 09:00–10:30 PDT window spiked and produced 3x higher latency than your perf report indicated on Tuesday.

Given the MAP acceptance gate is predicated on the evaluation window closing cleanly, we are not comfortable signing off on the original go-live date. We need to discuss either extending the evaluation window by two weeks to validate fixes or falling back to the previously approved model variant (which meets our compliance profile but has slightly higher latency).

Can you confirm next steps and whether Redwood can provide a short risk register and rollback options for our procurement/legal team to review? We have a procurement checkpoint scheduled next Friday — would like to keep that meeting productive rather than cancel it.

Thanks,
Lisa Ortega
Director, Platform Integrations
Acme Health

Attachment: acme-eval-logs.csv

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Ortega <lisa.ortega@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Eli Navarro <eli.navarro@partnercloud.com>
Date: 2026-10-20T10:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval window issues — possible go-live push?

Lisa — thank you for the details and for sending the logs. I pulled the team and we put together three near-term options (high level) for the MAP and go/no-go decision:

Option 1 — Short extension + targeted validation (preferred if root cause is isolated)
- Add 10 business days to the evaluation window focused on parity fixes and repeat traffic runs.
- Redwood will run an additional gated load test with your staging export and provide per-endpoint diffs.
- Risk: 10–14 day slip to close; low incremental cost.

Option 2 — Rollback to approved model variant (fastest to commit)
- Use the previously approved model variant used in the pilot (compliance-ok, slightly higher median latency).
- Allows go-live on the original date assuming procurement/legal accept the variance.
- Risk: measurable latency delta (P95 + 150–200ms), lower functional risk.

Option 3 — Canary + constrained acceptance (partial acceptance path)
- Staged rollout: 10% traffic canary on go-live; evaluation gate opens on observed behavior in production for 7 days.
- Requires an acceptance SLA and a rollback trigger in MAP.
- Risk: operational overhead and more complex rollback choreography.

I attached a short risk rollup (close-risk-rapsheet.xlsx) and an updated MAP draft (MAP-v3.xlsx) that adds a rollback clause and acceptance SLA for the canary path.

Ask: please confirm which option procurement/legal prefer to present at the Friday checkpoint. If procurement wants retained schedule, Option 2 is the path of least resistance. If Acme prefers to hold the original acceptance criteria, we should pursue Option 1. Option 3 is a compromise but will need exec alignment (we can operate it, but procurement must approve the acceptance SLA).

I propose a 30-minute exec sync Wednesday 9:30 PDT to lock to a path. Can you confirm availability?

Hannah Schmitt
Sr. Director, Strategic Accounts — Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0123

Attachments: close-risk-rapsheet.xlsx, MAP-v3.xlsx

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Lisa Ortega <lisa.ortega@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval window issues — possible go-live push?

Adding a technical/impact perspective and recommended short plan of action. TL;DR — Option 2 (rollback) minimizes calendar risk; Option 3 (canary) minimizes risk to production quality. I recommend preparing for Option 2 while planning Option 3 as fallback.

Minimal impact estimates (rough):
- Option 1 (10 business days): +12 business days impact to close; engineering validation effort ~ 2 FTE-weeks; estimated marginal infra cost ~$4k.
- Option 2 (rollback to pilot variant): 0–2 business days impact; config work ~ 0.5 FTE-days; negligible infra delta; latency tradeoff documented.
- Option 3 (canary): +3 business days for orchestration and acceptance SLA, ~1.5 FTE-weeks to instrument telemetry & rollback automation; ops on-call costs higher.

Proposed immediate actions (owners):
- Priyom (me): run a focused parity test against the failing queries by EOD Tuesday; produce per-endpoint diffs and a remediation checklist.
- Neha: draft the rollback/acceptance language for MAP-v3 and procurement; include explicit rollback triggers and owner contact list.
- Grace: prepare an exec summary slide (1 page) for Wednesday sync with cost/days/risk buckets.

If Procurement is firm about Friday’s checkpoint, we should present Option 2 as the recommended path but note that we can move to Option 3 if Acme wants staged exposure.

- Priyom
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Lisa Ortega <lisa.ortega@acmehealth.com>, Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T17:43:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Eval window issues — possible go-live push? 

Team — escalating to sales leadership and ops. We need a firm decision by EOD Friday (2026-10-23) so procurement can either greenlight the rollback or accept a 10-business-day extension. I have scheduled a 30-min decision meeting Friday 08:30 PDT and invited Markus and Marissa to join.

Quick notes:
- Priyom: make sure the parity report includes the two specific queries Lisa flagged and the exact row-count deltas; procurement will want numbers, not prose.
- Neha: populate the MAP acceptance SLA section and add an explicit rollback owner and contact method (PagerDuty + phone).
- Hannah: if Acme elects Option 2, we will prepare a short customer notice and amend the go-live checklist in HubSpot.

Links: HubSpot deal (https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-4932) — please update stage to "Decision - Escalated"; DocuSign LOI (https://docusign.com/ACME-4932-LOI) is currently unsigned and procurement needs visibility.

Grace O'Connor
VP, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
Phone: (650) 555-0199
